name: Sadalsuud
description: A supergiant of type G0 I 165 parsecs away, 47.9 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the Navy Precision Optical Interferometer.

radius.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 204867: radius 47.88 +1.81/-1.68 solar radii (Table 5), from the limb-darkened angular diameter 2.704 +/- 0.009 mas (NPOI, Table 4) and the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax

mass.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 204867: mass 4.97 +/- 0.1 solar masses (Table 6), from the PARAM Bayesian fit to PARSEC isochrones at the measured temperature; the paper calls its masses estimates only

temperature.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 204867: effective temperature 5608 +/- 71 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit

distance.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 204867: the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax the radius was computed with (Table 1), 6.07 +/- 0.22 mas, inverted

text.card: A supergiant of type G0 I, 165 parsecs away: 47.9 times the Sun's width and 2,046 times its light.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 2.704 milliarcseconds, which gives 47.88 solar radii and 5,608 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 1, 4 and 5, HD 204867: parallax, limb-darkened diameter, radius, Teff

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 2671038928727970944 (quality A), from 2018A&A...616A...7S; Gaia DR3 measures none
